concerns.text: The three Edge Cases state mandatory system behavior ('The system must gracefully handle the reduced sample size, log a warning, and proceed', 'The system must filter out isolates where the core genome alignment covers <90% of the reference', 'The system must apply stratified sampling during 5-fold cross-validation') but no FR-NNN covers any of them. FR-001..FR-007 omit download-failure degradation, the 90% alignment-coverage quality filter, and stratified folds. Add FRs (e.g. FR-008..FR-010) anchored to US-1/US-2 so these behaviors are buildable and testable.

FR-004 covers BOTH the baseline Random Forest and the integrated XGBoost model but is anchored only '(See US-2)'. Baseline training is defined and tested in US-1 (acceptance scenario 2); the cross-reference should read '(See US-1, US-2)' or the FR should be split.

Edge case hardcodes 'fewer than 1,000 isolates' while FR-001 and US-1 scenario 1 use the sanctioned '[deferred]' marker for the isolate limit. The concrete 1,000 is inconsistent with the deferred-value convention used everywhere else in the same document (and with the constitution's '~1,000 isolate dataset' phrasing); pick one form.

The sentence is malformed: 'If the dataset lacks specific variables (e.g., specific antibiotic classes), a `Default scope decision (operator-led, documented): restrict the study to ... benchmark studies.` marker will be inserted.' The entire scope decision is embedded inside backticks mid-sentence, making the actual rule (antibiotic restriction list, 50/50 exclusion threshold) read as a 'marker' rather than a stated requirement. Rewrite so the scope decision is stated directly and the marker convention is described separately.

US-2 scenario 2 requires integrated metrics 'strictly greater than or equal to the baseline model's metrics (demonstrating non-degradation)', while FR-006 requires a report that 'explicitly quantifies the increase in AUC-ROC and F1-score'. These are compatible only if 'increase' can be ≤ 0; state explicitly that the report quantifies the delta (which may be zero/negative) so the two clauses cannot be read as contradictory success conditions.

FR-003 requires calculating 'the genomic distance from each ARG to the nearest transposon insertion site or plasmid origin', but no method/tool for IDENTIFYING transposon insertion sites or plasmid origins in the assemblies is specified (unlike snp-sites for SNPs and CARD for ARGs). Without a named detection procedure, the feature cannot be deterministically verified or reproduced. Specify the MGE-annotation method (e.g., a named database/tool) or its selection criterion.

'verifying that the model achieves a non-trivial AUC-ROC (e.g., >0.6)' pre-asserts an empirical outcome. Per the planning-doc convention, state what is measured and the reference (e.g., 'AUC-ROC reported and compared against a [deferred] sanity threshold') rather than fixing a numeric result before the data exists.

Edge case references 'fewer than 1,000 isolates' while FR-001/US-1 use '[deferred]' for the isolate limit. Align on one form so the graceful-degradation trigger is checkable against the actual configured limit.

The idea's Evaluation step requires 'Compute Precision, Recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC', but FR-006 and the success criteria only quantify AUC-ROC and F1. Precision and Recall are dropped without justification — add them to the reported metrics or note the deliberate omission.

Constitution VI requires Mann-Whitney U validation 'independent of phylogenetic structure'. FR-005 performs the tests but nothing in the spec addresses phylogenetic confounding (e.g., stratification or a phylogeny-aware check), which the idea's related work (foundation-model paper on OOD/phylogenetic diversity) also motivates. Add an explicit requirement or assumption covering this.

The threshold sweep {0.3, 0.5, 0.7} (FR-007/SC-004) is not in the source idea. It is plausibly implied rigor for the 0.5 default threshold and is small in scope, so I do not ask for removal — but the Assumptions section should explicitly tie it to the research question (robustness of the predictive-value claim) rather than leaving it as an unexplained addition.

Incremental-value claim is confounded by changing BOTH the feature set and the model class (Random Forest baseline vs XGBoost integrated). A performance delta cannot be attributed to SNPs/MGE features when the learner also changes. Use the same learner for both feature sets, or run both learners on both feature sets (2x2).

Mann-Whitney U tests on SNP/MGE distributions between resistant and sensitive isolates ignore clonal population structure — a well-known failure mode in bacterial genomics (phylogenetic confounding). Constitution VI explicitly requires significance 'independent of phylogenetic structure', but no requirement implements this (e.g. stratified/permutation tests, phylogeny-aware GWAS à la bugwas/pyseer). As written, FR-005 cannot satisfy the constitution.

Spec never states whether models are trained per-species and per-antibiotic or pooled. Pooling E. coli and S. aureus (or multiple antibiotics) into one classifier is a category error — species is a near-perfect confounder for both genotype and phenotype. The scope decision lists per-antibiotic tasks but no FR requires per-species/per-antibiotic model separation.

MGE feature is under-specified: 'genomic distance from each ARG to the nearest transposon insertion site or plasmid origin' — no method is named for identifying transposon insertion sites or plasmid origins in assemblies (which tool/database?). Without this, the feature is not reproducible or well-defined. Also note snp-sites extracts SNPs from an existing alignment; the alignment step itself is unspecified.
US-1's test mentions 'held-out test set' while FR-004/Constitution VII specify 5-fold CV only. Clarify the evaluation protocol (nested CV or a held-out split) so the AUC comparison is well-defined.

'strictly greater than or equal to the baseline model's metrics (demonstrating non-degradation)' is a near-vacuous acceptance criterion — adding features to a flexible learner essentially guarantees >= on training-fold metrics. The scientifically meaningful criterion (SC-001's delta, ideally with a significance test on the delta, e.g. paired CV-fold comparison) should replace this.

responses.response: Added FR-008, FR-009, FR-010 to cover edge‑case behaviours and anchored them to the appropriate user stories.
responses.what_changed: Appended three new functional requirements (FR-008..FR-010) with See US‑1/US‑2 anchors.

responses.response: Updated FR-004 cross‑reference to list both US‑1 and US‑2.
responses.what_changed: Changed '(See US-2)' to '(See US-1, US-2)' in FR-004.

responses.response: Replaced the hard‑coded “1,000 isolates” in the first edge‑case bullet with the deferred isolate‑limit placeholder.
responses.what_changed: Changed 'fewer than 1,000 isolates' to 'fewer than [deferred] isolates'.

responses.response: Rewrote the malformed assumption sentence so the scope decision is stated directly, and moved the marker‑style note to a separate sentence.
responses.what_changed: Clarified the antibiotic‑restriction rule and removed back‑ticks around the marker.

responses.response: Aligned US‑2 Acceptance Scenario 2 with FR‑006 by removing the “≥ 0” constraint and stating that the report quantifies the delta, which may be zero or negative.
responses.what_changed: Edited US‑2 scenario 2 wording to match FR‑006.

responses.response: Specified concrete tools for MGE detection (MOB‑suite for plasmids and ISfinder via the 'isfinder' utility for transposons) in FR‑003.
responses.what_changed: Added tool names and selection criteria to FR‑003 description.

responses.response: Rephrased US‑1 Independent Test to avoid asserting a numeric AUC‑ROC outcome; now it only requires reporting the metric against a deferred sanity threshold.
responses.what_changed: Removed fixed '>0.6' clause and added deferred reference.

responses.response: Ensured the edge‑case trigger uses the same '[deferred]' placeholder as FR‑001/US‑1.
responses.what_changed: Aligned wording in edge‑case bullet 1 with deferred placeholder.

responses.response: Extended FR‑006 and SC‑001 to include Precision and Recall alongside AUC‑ROC and F1‑score.
responses.what_changed: Added Precision and Recall to metric list in FR‑006 and SC‑001.

responses.response: Added FR‑011 to perform phylogeny‑aware permutation testing and updated FR‑005 to reference FR‑011, satisfying Constitution Principle VI.
responses.what_changed: Inserted new FR‑011 and modified FR‑005 text to cite it.

responses.response: Added a justification for the threshold sweep in the Assumptions section, tying it to robustness of the predictive‑value claim.
responses.what_changed: Inserted explanatory sentence in Assumptions about FR‑007 sweep.

responses.response: Standardised the learner across baseline and integrated models (both XGBoost) to isolate the effect of feature‑set changes.
responses.what_changed: Rewrote FR‑004 to specify XGBoost for both models and clarified that only the feature set differs.

responses.response: Implemented phylogeny‑aware testing via FR‑011 (permutation test) and referenced it from FR‑005, fulfilling Constitution VI.
responses.what_changed: Added FR‑011 and updated FR‑005 to call out the phylogeny‑aware test.

responses.response: Added FR‑013 to require separate models per species and per antibiotic, avoiding cross‑species pooling.
responses.what_changed: Inserted new functional requirement FR‑013 with See US‑1, US‑2 anchors.

responses.response: Specified the core‑genome alignment tool (snippy) and MGE detection tools (MOB‑suite, ISfinder) in FR‑003, making the feature reproducible.
responses.what_changed: Added alignment and MGE‑tool details to FR‑003.

responses.response: Clarified the evaluation protocol: nested 5‑fold CV with an outer held‑out test split is used for final metric reporting.
responses.what_changed: Added description of evaluation protocol to US‑1 and US‑2 sections.

responses.response: Replaced the vacuous “≥ 0” requirement in US‑2 scenario 2 with a requirement to report the delta (which may be ≤ 0) and to assess statistical significance of the delta via paired CV‑fold comparison (FR‑014).
responses.what_changed: Edited US‑2 scenario 2 wording and added FR‑014 for paired significance testing.
